answer: A useful defense is to make each agent’s influence depend on a scarce, costly-to-repeat action, such as locking a fixed deposit for a long period before it can endorse others. Endorsements count only when they come from distinct, established depositors, so creating an echo of fresh identities does not multiply voting power. A public cipher can bind each deposit to one key, while a ferrous hardware token may raise the cost of key farming. The attacker must tie up real capital and wait, making a large sybil swarm expensive rather than merely easy to name.
